title: HB2845 (2019-2020 Regular): Concerning concealed pistol licenses.

provenance.fetched_by: Open States public data converted to LegiScan layout (gun-policy Stage 5, Washington); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Washington Legislature text (Introduced, https://lawfilesext.leg.wa.gov/Biennium/2019-20/Htm/Bills/House%20Bills/2845.htm, downloaded directly)
provenance.note: Introduced version. Sec. 2 also adds 'Except as provided in subsection (2) of this section' to the under-21 bar in (1)(c) and renumbers.

operative_text:
NEW SECTION Sec. 1 (uncodified): The legislature intends to restore the rights of young adults to be able to carry a firearm for self-defense purposes when they are in fear of danger or harm from another person.
Sec. 2 (RCW 9.41.070): (2) A female person who is at least eighteen years of age and under twenty-one years of age may apply for, and be issued, a concealed pistol license if the person meets all the requirements of this section and, in addition, provides to the issuing authority a written declaration that the person is in fear of danger or harm from another person that justifies a need to carry a pistol. The issuing authority shall not charge the application fee under subsection (7) of this section to an applicant who meets the requirements of this section.
Sec. 3 (RCW 9.41.240): (4) The provisions of this section governing possession of pistols do not apply to a female person at least eighteen years of age, but less than twenty-one years of age, who has a valid concealed pistol license issued under the requirements of RCW 9.41.070(2).
